puzzles.title: Acid-base disorders

groups.category: Causes of high anion gap metabolic acidosis
groups.explain: Unmeasured anions (formate, glycolate, lactate, ketones) raise the anion gap.
Hypoventilation retains CO2, whether from drive, airway or muscle failure.
Volume contraction, chloride loss, mineralocorticoid excess or alkali load generate bicarbonate.

groups.category: Causes of normal anion gap (hyperchloremic) acidosis
groups.explain: Bicarbonate loss (GI or renal) with chloride retention leaves the gap normal.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Acetazolamide and Loop diuretics both sound like diuretics but one causes NAGMA and one alkalosis; Diarrhea sounds like fluid loss/alkalosis. Least sure: Milk-alkali syndrome (also causes hypercalcemia, still alkalosis).

puzzles.title: Drug adverse effects: set 1

groups.explain: ACE inhibitors raise bradykinin (cough, angioedema) and reduce aldosterone (hyperkalemia).
Loops waste K, Mg and Ca, compete with urate secretion and can damage the cochlea.
Statins cause muscle toxicity, transaminase rise and a small increase in diabetes risk.
Amiodarone is lipophilic and deposits in lung, cornea and skin.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Hyperkalemia vs Hypokalemia; Rhabdomyolysis and Ototoxicity could be mis-sorted. Least sure: Hyperuricemia (loop effect via urate competition, well established); Photosensitivity (also occurs with other drugs, but valid for amiodarone).

puzzles.title: Electrolyte culprits

groups.explain: Hyperparathyroidism and malignancy account for most hypercalcemia; granulomas make calcitriol.
Aldosterone or ENaC blockade, depolarizing paralytics and Na/K-ATPase inhibition all raise K.
GI loss, renal wasting and beta-agonist cellular shift all lower serum K.
Low PTH or vitamin D, saponification in pancreatitis and citrate chelation lower ionized calcium.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Spironolactone (diuretic, sounds like K loss) is hyperkalemia; Amphotericin B and Bartter are K wasters. Dropped thiazides and rhabdomyolysis because they fit two groups. Least sure: Digoxin toxicity (acute toxicity raises K).

puzzles.title: Valve and murmur findings

groups.explain: Large stroke volume with diastolic runoff produces the peripheral signs of AR.
A stenotic mitral leaflet snaps open and produces a low-pitched diastolic rumble.
Fixed outflow obstruction gives a late, weak pulse and an ejection murmur radiating to the neck.
Reduced preload worsens dynamic LVOT obstruction in HOCM.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: AS vs HCM (both systolic murmurs); Widened vs Narrow pulse pressure. Dropped ejection murmur, syncope, paradoxical S2, LA enlargement (shared). Least sure: Soft single S2 for AS (severe, calcific AS).

puzzles.title: Pleura and lung

groups.explain: Inflammation or malignancy increases capillary permeability and protein in pleural fluid.
Hydrostatic or oncotic pressure shifts create protein-poor fluid.
Reduced FEV1/FVC defines obstruction.
Reduced lung volumes with preserved FEV1/FVC define restriction.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Pancreatitis (abdominal, sounds like transudative ascites) is exudative. Least sure: Peritoneal dialysis as transudate (uncommon but classic teaching); Malignancy (occasionally transudative).

puzzles.title: Endocrine culprits

groups.explain: Glucocorticoid excess is most often iatrogenic; then ACTH-dependent and adrenal causes.
Autonomous hormone production or excess intake produces thyrotoxicosis with low TSH.
Autoimmune destruction, iodine lack, ablation or lithium reduce hormone output.
Destruction of cortex or loss of ACTH drive causes cortisol deficiency.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: ACTH-secreting pituitary tumor vs Pituitary apoplexy; Exogenous steroids (can suppress axis). Dropped amiodarone and subacute thyroiditis (fit both thyroid groups). Least sure: ACTH-secreting pituitary tumor (a macroadenoma can cause hypopituitarism, but this item is Cushing disease).

puzzles.title: Kidney patterns

groups.explain: Podocyte or basement membrane injury causes heavy proteinuria.
Inflammatory glomerular injury gives hematuria, RBC casts and hypertension.
Ischemia and tubular toxins injure tubular cells, leaving muddy brown casts.
Drug hypersensitivity causes interstitial inflammation with WBC casts and eosinophils.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Aminoglycosides and NSAIDs sound like AIN but aminoglycosides cause ATN; NSAIDs deliberately excluded. Least sure: IgA nephropathy (can be nephrotic rarely); Diabetic nephropathy placement.

puzzles.title: Liver and pancreas

groups.explain: Massive hepatocyte injury gives ALT/AST in the thousands.
Portal hypertension and liver failure drive these complications.
Gallstones and alcohol dominate; metabolic, procedural and drug causes follow.
Bile duct injury or obstruction raises ALP and GGT out of proportion to ALT.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Choledocholithiasis (gallstones sound like a pancreatitis cause). Dropped alcohol, gallstones, pancreatic head cancer (valid in multiple groups). Least sure: Herpes simplex hepatitis (rare, classically over 1000).

puzzles.title: Infections by category

groups.explain: Atypicals are not seen on Gram stain and are not covered by beta-lactams.
Common enteric pathogens by exposure.
Encapsulated organisms need splenic opsonization for clearance.
Advanced HIV allows these to emerge as CD4 falls.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Klebsiella and Legionella both cause pneumonia but only Klebsiella is an encapsulated bacterium; Salmonella dropped (encapsulated and diarrheal). Least sure: Primary CNS lymphoma (a neoplasm, category worded loosely); Coxiella as atypical.

puzzles.title: Neurologic signs

groups.explain: Dopaminergic loss produces the parkinsonian tetrad.
Cerebellar lesions cause ataxia and dysmetria.
Loss of descending inhibition produces spastic weakness.
Anterior horn or nerve injury produces flaccid weakness with atrophy.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Resting vs Intention tremor; Hyperreflexia vs Hyporeflexia; Cogwheel rigidity vs Spasticity. Least sure: Nystagmus (also vestibular but valid cerebellar).

puzzles.title: Anemia and blood counts

groups.explain: Reduced hemoglobin synthesis gives small red cells.
Impaired DNA synthesis or toxins enlarge red cells.
Red-cell destruction raises LDH and indirect bilirubin and lowers haptoglobin.
Hypoxia or EPO excess raises red cell mass.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Hydroxyurea is used in sickle cell (sounds hemolytic) but causes macrocytosis. Least sure: Alpha-thalassemia trait (mild hemolysis possible), Lead poisoning (can be normocytic).

puzzles.title: Joint pain

groups.explain: HLA-B27-associated arthropathies without rheumatoid factor.
Monosodium urate deposition causes gout.
Calcium pyrophosphate crystals deposit in cartilage.
Inflammation of vessel walls, classified by vessel size.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: crystal findings (negative vs positive birefringence, needle vs rhomboid) trade places easily. Least sure: Hemochromatosis as a pseudogout association (established), Hyperuricemia (not specific but gout group).

puzzles.title: Toxidromes and antidotes

groups.explain: Mu agonism causes miosis, hypoventilation, reduced gut motility and sedation.
Blocked muscarinic signaling: dry as a bone, blind as a bat, mad as a hatter.
Salicylate stimulates the respiratory center and uncouples oxidative phosphorylation.
Specific agents reverse opioids, benzodiazepines, toxic alcohols and cyanide.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Naloxone sounds like part of the opioid toxidrome but is an antidote; Hyperthermia is shared by salicylate toxicity but listed as anticholinergic. Least sure: Hyperthermia (also in salicylate toxicity), Hypoactive bowel sounds.

puzzles.title: ECG patterns

groups.explain: Progressive hyperkalemia flattens atrial activity and widens QRS to a sine wave.
Epicardial inflammation causes diffuse ST/PR changes and positional pain.
Low K delays repolarization and exposes U waves.
Acute right heart strain produces right-sided ECG changes.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Widened QRS vs New RBBB; Friction rub is an exam sign rather than an ECG finding (category worded for acute pericarditis). Least sure: Frequent PVCs for hypokalemia; Apparent QT prolongation.

puzzles.title: Diabetes drug classes

groups.explain: The -gliflozins block renal glucose reabsorption.
Incretin mimetics: -glutide and -natide.
The -gliptins prolong endogenous incretin action.
Insulin secretagogues that risk hypoglycemia.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys are the look-alike suffixes (-gliflozin, -gliptin, -glutide, -gli-). Least sure: none; all are standard class memberships.

puzzles.title: Antibiotic adverse effects

groups.explain: Fluoroquinolones carry boxed warnings for tendon, nerve and CNS effects.
Dose-dependent toxicity of cochlea, vestibule, kidney and neuromuscular junction.
Tetracyclines bind calcium and irritate the esophagus.
Linezolid is a weak MAO inhibitor and inhibits mitochondrial protein synthesis.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Ototoxicity and Cartilage damage easily swap; Peripheral vs Optic neuropathy between FQ and linezolid. Least sure: Impaired bone growth (tetracycline in children, standard); Aortic aneurysm risk for FQ (FDA warning).

puzzles.title: Blood pressure patterns

groups.explain: Identifiable endocrine, renal or vascular causes.
Fluid retention, vasoconstriction or increased viscosity raise BP.
Large stroke volume with low diastolic runoff widens the pulse pressure.
Low stroke volume narrows the pulse pressure.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Hyperthyroidism dropped (raises systolic BP and widens pulse pressure). Least sure: Severe anemia for wide pulse pressure; Cyclosporine hypertension.

puzzles.title: Shock types

groups.explain: Vasodilation drops SVR.
Pump failure reduces cardiac output with high filling pressures.
A physical obstruction limits venous return or outflow.
Loss of intravascular volume lowers preload.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Cardiac tamponade (sounds cardiac) is obstructive; Toxic shock syndrome overlaps septic shock but both distributive. Least sure: Auto-PEEP (obstructive by impaired venous return); Severe burns (hypovolemic with distributive component).

puzzles.title: Drug-induced syndromes

groups.category: Drugs that prolong the QT interval
groups.explain: HERG potassium channel blockade lengthens repolarization.
Antiandrogen or estrogen-like effects cause breast tissue growth.
ADH release or potentiation causes euvolemic hyponatremia.
Anti-histone antibodies appear; procainamide is classic but also prolongs QT.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Dropped procainamide (lupus and QT) and ketoconazole (QT and gynecomastia). Least sure: Sertraline for SIADH (SSRIs generally, valid); Digoxin gynecomastia.

puzzles.title: Chemotherapy toxicities

groups.explain: Cisplatin injures proximal tubules and the cochlea.
Lung is the dose-limiting organ for bleomycin.
Anthracyclines cause dose-related cardiomyopathy.
Acrolein injures bladder urothelium; mesna binds it.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Pulmonary fibrosis vs cardiomyopathy as organ-specific toxicity. Least sure: Secondary leukemia for doxorubicin; Hypomagnesemia (valid for cisplatin).

puzzles.title: Vector-borne and zoonotic

groups.explain: Ixodes, Dermacentor and Amblyomma ticks transmit these.
Anopheles and Aedes/Culex mosquitoes are the vectors.
Fleas and body lice transmit these.

groups.category: Direct animal exposure without arthropod vector
groups.explain: Livestock, rodents, birds or hides transmit these directly.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Typhus and RMSF are both rickettsial but have different vectors; Plague is zoonotic but flea-borne. Least sure: Anthrax and Plague boundaries; Anaplasmosis (Ixodes ticks).

puzzles.title: Chest pain differential

groups.explain: Pericardial inflammation causes positional pleuritic pain.
Venous thromboembolism risk factors and infarct signs point to PE.
Intimal tear findings affect pulses, imaging and the aortic valve.
Forceful emesis ruptures the distal esophagus.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Dropped pleuritic pain (pericarditis and PE) and sinus tachycardia. Least sure: Hampton hump (PE infarct sign); Left pleural effusion for Boerhaave.

puzzles.title: Hyperglycemic emergencies and adrenal crisis

groups.explain: Ketone accumulation causes gap acidosis and compensatory hyperventilation.
Severe hyperglycemia and osmolality with little ketosis.
Mineralocorticoid excess wastes K and H and suppresses renin.
Cortisol and aldosterone deficiency produce these abnormalities.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Hypokalemia vs Hyperkalemia; Hyperglycemia dropped from DKA items (shared with HHS). Least sure: Low bicarbonate/Bicarbonate over 18 thresholds; Eosinophilia in adrenal insufficiency.

puzzles.title: Hyponatremia by mechanism

groups.explain: Volume depletion drives ADH release and water retention.
Low effective arterial volume causes ADH release.
Impaired water excretion without edema or volume depletion.

groups.category: Hyponatremia with normal or high osmolality
groups.explain: Osmotic water shifts or lab artifact lower measured sodium.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Addison disease (endocrine, sounds euvolemic) is hypovolemic; Hypothyroidism vs Cirrhosis. Least sure: Hypothyroidism (euvolemic, debated mechanism); Advanced CKD.

puzzles.title: Infective endocarditis

groups.explain: Embolic and immune phenomena appear in the skin, nails and retina.
Skin, oral and gut flora are the usual culprits.
Bacteremia plus an abnormal surface or foreign material predisposes.
Local invasion and embolization cause the major complications.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Staph aureus and Injection drug use are linked but belong to different groups; Janeway lesions vs Septic emboli. Least sure: Hemodialysis catheter as a risk factor; New PR prolongation (marker of abscess).

puzzles.title: Antithrombotic drugs

groups.explain: These block platelet ADP signaling.
Direct or indirect factor Xa inhibition.
These bind thrombin directly.
Plasminogen activators dissolve clot.

puzzles.review_notes: Decoys: Dabigatran (a DOAC) sits with thrombin inhibitors, not the Xa DOACs; Fondaparinux is a parenteral Xa inhibitor. Least sure: Fondaparinux (indirect via antithrombin).
